story_text.value:
Hey HN,

First time building SaaS. Don't be too harsh, but I would appreciate your feedback. I have a strong technical background, but never had an opportunity to design as much as a landing page or think about product positioning. If you see something that's an obvious gap, please take a second to leave a comment.

Now, the product:

I use MCPs. I've worked in teams that use MCPs. Regardless of whether you are 1 or many, these are the issues that you will run into:

* random API keys in .env files

* OAuth credentials that expire

* no visibility of which MCPs are used

* no controls over what data is being sent to MCPs

There are also nice-to-haves that you wish you've had:

* hosting/sharing private MCP tools

* fixing context bloat

MCP gateways are designed to solve these problems. However, in my experience, they are expensive and hard to use. Everything that I've tried felt like it was designed by someone who can conceptualize the problem, but hasn't experienced it. Whereas I have seen it working for a big team and also trying to setup my own development environment. And that's Rayrun – an MCP gateway that solves hosting, data governance, secrets, OAuth rotation, and gives visibility across your organization. It's designed to be useful whether you are solo or a 500 people team.

I would truly appreciate you giving it a try and ask any questions or share observations.

If you are curious about feature parity with the existing MCP gateways, I've made a comparison matrix https://ray.run/compare

title.value: Show HN: Rayrun – one MCP gateway for the whole company

story_text.value:
The other week I posted a concept to use the macOS Accessibility API to capture the text on your screen into a markdown file. It seemed to be interesting with 150+ github stars.

I've done a bunch of updates and packaged them into a signed macOS app.

One of the biggest changes was moving away from 'one context file per day' to three markdown files for apps, website, and messages.

I then run Andrej Karpathy's LLM Wiki process to turn into a simple knowledge base for the day. This is then used by a smarter model to synthesise into a daily overview.

Let me know what you think

Original: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49429095

title.value: Show HN: Ambient Context v1.0.0 (Missing context for AI assistants)

story_text.value:
I was playing around with embedding models and I realized the moving between embedding models on a large corpus can cause a huge backfill, as all of the previous documents would have to be re embedded.

embedflow tries to forgo that; it takes candidate documents from the previous index, and reranks them in realtime with the new model. It supports faiss, qdrant, and pgvector

people who have migrated large production vector indexes, would this be helpful for you?

title.value: Show HN: EmbedFlow –> Upgrade embedding models without re-embedding your corpus

story_text.value:
I built CantonPay because I wanted a simple way to accept Stellar payments without creating a merchant account.

You can create a payment link without registering, send it to someone, and receive the payment directly to your Stellar wallet.

It also has an API and webhooks for integrating payments into an application.

The current version is running on Stellar Testnet, so there’s no real money involved.

I’d especially like feedback from developers who have built payment flows on Stellar.

title.value: Show HN: CantonPay – registration-free Stellar payment links
